title: Multi-tier health scoring and request-shape circuit breakers to stabilize autoscaling
creator: Rajiv Patel
description:
Problem: Large, bursty inference requests (long token sequences and heavy batching) combined with region failovers are causing repeated autoscaler thrash and transient p99 latency regressions for customer routes that have strict SLOs. Existing health signals are binary and per-host; they do not account for request shape (short chat vs long generation) or workload tail behavior, which prevents the autoscaler and regional circuit breakers from making SLO-aware decisions.

Goal: Implement a multi-tier health scoring system and request-shape-aware circuit breakers that drive more stable autoscaling decisions and controlled load shedding during overloads or partial-region outages, while minimizing customer-visible SLO regressions. The system should: 1) surface graded health per node and per pool (fast/slow/pressure tiers), 2) let circuit breakers preferentially degrade long-token/low-importance requests first, and 3) provide autoscaler damping and hysteresis informed by these graded signals to prevent thrash.

Constraints: Must integrate with existing serving runtime (KV cache, batcher), be region-aware for multi-region failover, and be deployable behind a feature flag. Implementation should avoid per-request expensive computation and prefer lightweight counters, exponentially weighted averages, and configurable bucketing of request shapes.

Proposed solution:
- Health scoring tiers:
  - Tier A (immediate readiness): low-latency short-request success rate, RAM and GPU memory headroom > threshold.
  - Tier B (SLO-expectation): moving-window tail latency bucket score (p95/p99 grouped by request-length buckets), small queue-depth estimate.
  - Tier C (pressure): resource pressure score derived from GPU utilization gradients, batch queue growth rate, and KV cache miss pressure.
- Request shape classification: cheap in-proxy classification into shape buckets: small (<=64 tokens), medium (65-1024), large (>1024), plus I/O-bound vs compute-bound flags when available.
- Circuit breaker semantics: per-route, per-model-variant breakers that consume the multi-tier score and request-shape to decide actions: pass, deprioritize (lower scheduling weight), reject-with-backoff, or shed tokens (throttle long requests first). Breaker incorporates hysteresis windows and exponential backoff on flip.
- Autoscaler integration: health scores aggregated to pool-level SLO health metric. Autoscaler applies derivative damping and minimum stable window (configurable) before scaling decisions. When breakers are active, autoscaler uses a conservative scaling profile to avoid up/down oscillation.
- Observability and runbook: add dashboards for per-bucket latency, health-tier distributions, breaker flips, and autoscaler decisions. Add an automated alert when pool-level SLO health drops below X for Y minutes.

Trade-offs:
- Benefits: fewer autoscaler thrash events, controlled degradation prioritizing short-interactive requests, predictable failover behavior.
- Costs: extra telemetry and complexity, possible reduction in throughput for long-batch workloads in degraded mode.

Rollout plan: start with a canary on non-critical routes in us-west-2, validate metrics, then expand to blue/green regions. Feature flag to allow immediate rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Deployable behind feature flag and enabled for a single pool via config
Per-pool health-tier metrics emitted (Tier A/B/C) with <10s update latency
Circuit breaker actions (deprioritize/reject/shed) can be exercised by synthetic traffic and observed in dashboards
Autoscaler thrash count (scale up followed by scale down within 5m) reduced by >=70% for test workload compared to baseline
No regression in short-request p99 latency for enabled routes (<=5% change) under normal load
Failover scenario: when region B becomes degraded, primary region failover completes without >2x increase in customer error rate within 60s for short-chat routes
Runbook created with steps to disable breakers or revert health scoring within 15 minutes
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit tests + integration tests in CI; gather baseline metrics for representative routes
Phase 1: Canary in us-west-2 on non-critical customer routes (1% traffic) behind feature flag for 48h
Phase 2: Expand to 10% traffic and enable autoscaler damping (monitor thrash and tail latency) for 72h
Phase 3: Multi-region chaos run (simulate region slowdowns/failures) in staging to validate cross-region breaker and failover behavior
Phase 4: Gradual rollout to all regions with per-region rollout windows and runbook gate
monitoring_signals: per-route p50/p95/p99 grouped by request-size bucket
health-tier counts and ratios (Tier A/B/C) per pool and per region
breaker flip rate and current state (open/closed/degrading) per route
autoscaler action log (scale events with reason and pre/post pool size)
GPU utilization gradients and batch queue growth rate
synthetic transaction success latency by bucket
customer error rate and rate-limited rejects
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and hysteresis windows
Load tests with mix of small/medium/large requests to validate prioritized shedding behavior
Chaos tests: kill subset of hosts in a region and observe breaker flips and autoscaler damping behavior
Regression tests to ensure short-request p99 does not increase under normal load
End-to-end smoke: enable on a canary route and run synthetic transactions for 24h
updates: 2026-02-11: Triage - scoped problem to long-token workloads and autoscaler thrash; assigned to Mei. Rajiv added baseline metrics for affected routes.
2026-02-18: Design review with SRE and PM (Lina Torres). PM requested explicit customer impact gating and synthetic transaction coverage for short-chat routes.
2026-02-25: Prototype scoring service pushed to branch (see PR). Prototype uses EWMA for p99 buckets and lightweight queue-growth estimator.
2026-03-03: SRE requested hysteresis window increase to 45s to avoid flips during transient GC storms; adjusted default in branch.
2026-03-10: Canary started in us-west-2 (1% traffic). Early observation: breaker flip count is stable and short-request p99 unchanged. Continuing canary run.
